Hi Sabrina — Kimberly here, diving into the technical bits. Below is a short narrative we plan to include in the packet; I've also attached a draft diagram (orchid-isolation-diagram-v1.pdf) and a control mapping spreadsheet (sig-control-mapping-table.xlsx). Please treat the diagram as draft — we'll adjust after your CIDR/key preferences.

Draft narrative (summary):
- Dedicated GPU pool: Orchid's workloads run on a logically-isolated GPU pool backed by reserved capacity. Compute isolation is enforced through tenant routing and process sandboxing inside the inference runtime.
- Control plane separation: The customer-facing data path (inference requests/response) terminates at the dedicated serving nodes. Control plane operations (deploys, scaling) are executed through a private control plane endpoint per-customer; cross-tenant management operations are separated by RBAC and service tokens.
- Network segregation: We provide VPC peering or private link options — traffic crosses a dedicated interface with strict egress ACLs enforced at the edge. Egress is routed through a customer-configurable NAT or an inspection proxy; we can lock egress to specific destinations.
- KMS and key handling: We support two patterns: Redwood-managed KMS with customer-supplied key material (BYOK) and customer-managed KMS through a VPC connector (customer HSM). The packet will list the required key creation and rotation steps.
- Tenant fencing: KV-cache and model state are namespaced per-tenant. At the hypervisor/container boundary we employ memory isolation and explicit cache eviction between tenant contexts to prevent leakage.

Open items we need from Orchid to finalize the artifacts:
1) Network CIDR(s) to include on diagrams
2) Preference for KMS pattern (Redwood BYOK vs customer-managed)
3) Any regulatory-specific wording your legal/compliance team prefers for PHI-adjacent workloads

Workshop: Thu 19 Mar, 09:00–09:45 PT (we can extend if needed). I'll run the diagram and control mapping live and capture any redlines.

Thanks — attaching draft files now.
